title: How To Build A $1M One-Person Business Faster With AI

sentences.en: A question I've been thinking about a lot recently is how do you build a one person business in 2026?
sentences.zh: 我最近一直在想一个问题：2026 年怎么打造一个一人企业？

sentences.en: If you followed me last year or the year before.
sentences.zh: 如果你去年或前年关注过我。

sentences.en: You know that one person businesses were very popular and my videos on those did really well.
sentences.zh: 你知道一人企业当时非常火，我那些视频数据也特别好。

sentences.en: So did anything change from those videos?
sentences.zh: 那这些视频里的东西变了吗？

sentences.en: I was taking over everything.
sentences.zh: 我当时几乎包揽了一切。

sentences.en: Agents new features are launching literally every day on Twitter.
sentences.zh: 现在 Twitter 上每天都有新的 Agent 功能发布。

sentences.en: What's changed?
sentences.zh: 到底变了什么？

sentences.en: How do you actually use this stuff if you're going to use it?
sentences.zh: 如果你要用这些东西，到底该怎么用？

sentences.en: And just what does the one person business landscape look like now?
sentences.zh: 以及现在一人企业的格局到底是什么样的？

sentences.en: So to get straight to the point and answer the question, how do you build a one person business in 2026?
sentences.zh: 直接说重点，回答这个问题：2026 年怎么打造一个一人企业？

sentences.en: You do the same thing that you would have done before, but now you use AI to enhance that process, right?
sentences.zh: 你做的事跟以前一样，但现在你用 AI 来加速这个过程，对吧？

sentences.en: You don't really need a course or a coach anymore, although those things are still valuable because there's specific knowledge that you probably wouldn't think to look up with AI, or even do with AI in the AI probably isn't going to give you that out of the box.
sentences.zh: 你不再真的需要一门课程或一个教练了，虽然这些东西仍然有价值，因为有些特定知识你可能根本不会想到用 AI 去查，甚至不会用 AI 去做，而且 AI 大概率也不会直接给你现成的答案。

sentences.en: So courses are still going to be a thing.
sentences.zh: 所以课程依然会存在。

sentences.en: Coaching is still going to be a thing.
sentences.zh: 教练也依然会存在。

sentences.en: Just because the default response of the AI usually isn't that good.
sentences.zh: 纯粹是因为 AI 的默认回答通常不够好。

sentences.en: Getting specific knowledge from the source of someone who's done something is still superior.
sentences.zh: 从真正做成过某件事的人那里获取特定知识，仍然是更优的选择。

sentences.en: And if it cost 25 to 100 to 200 bucks, big whoop.
sentences.zh: 如果花 25 到 100 到 200 美元，那又怎样呢。

sentences.en: So to build the business with AI, you just implement AI in the correct places so that you can do things faster with higher quality and without less guesswork.
sentences.zh: 所以用 AI 打造企业，你只需要在正确的地方嵌入 AI，让你能做得更快、质量更高、少走弯路。

sentences.en: AI, in this sense, is a catalyst to avoid a lot of trial and error, so you can still build a business the old way.
sentences.zh: 从这个意义上说，AI 是一种催化剂，帮你避开大量试错，所以你仍然可以用老方法打造企业。

sentences.en: That's fine.
sentences.zh: 那也没问题。

sentences.en: It'll just take a bit longer, especially if you're not a person who is high agency or knows how to iterate or refine or not.
sentences.zh: 只是会多花一点时间，尤其是如果你不是一个主观能动性很强、或者不知道怎么迭代优化的人。

sentences.en: Just accept the output of AI as law.
sentences.zh: 别把 AI 的输出当成真理。

sentences.en: So what will you still do to build a one person business?
sentences.zh: 那么打造一人企业，你仍然要做哪些事？

sentences.en: You will still generate traffic.
sentences.zh: 你仍然要获取流量。

sentences.en: You still write content, you still write emails or newsletters.
sentences.zh: 你仍然要写内容，仍然要写邮件或 newsletter。

sentences.en: You still create a product or service.
sentences.zh: 你仍然要创建一个产品或服务。

sentences.en: You still create a customer avatar.
sentences.zh: 你仍然要构建客户画像。

sentences.en: You still formulate a compelling offer.
sentences.zh: 你仍然要打磨一个有吸引力的 offer。

sentences.en: You still build a landing page.
sentences.zh: 你仍然要搭建落地页。

sentences.en: You still write persuasive copy for that page.
sentences.zh: 你仍然要为那个页面写有说服力的文案。

sentences.en: You still put the offer in front of people and see if they buy, and then you iterate from there.
sentences.zh: 你仍然要把 offer 推到人们面前，看他们会不会买，然后从这里开始迭代。

sentences.en: After all of that, now that's a lot of stuff, right?
sentences.zh: 做完所有这些，工作量不小，对吧？

sentences.en: As a one person business, you are the marketing department.
sentences.zh: 作为一人企业，你就是市场部。

sentences.en: You are the sales department.
sentences.zh: 你就是销售部。

sentences.en: You're the product lead, you're the project manager, you're the content writer, you're the social media strategist.
sentences.zh: 你是产品负责人，你是项目经理，你是内容写手，你是社交媒体策略师。

sentences.en: You have to learn so many things and you have to become a generalist.
sentences.zh: 你得学太多东西了，你必须成为一个通才。

sentences.en: Even though people tell you to niche down, you still need the general skills to build the business.
sentences.zh: 即使别人告诉你要细分定位，你仍然需要通用技能来搭建这个生意。

sentences.en: But that's just the thing.
sentences.zh: 但问题就在这里。

sentences.en: Before AI, social media was the technology that allowed such a one person business to exist.
sentences.zh: 在 AI 出现之前，社交媒体是让这种一人企业得以存在的技术。

sentences.en: But you could create a comfortable lifestyle business.
sentences.zh: 但你能创建的只是一个舒适的生活方式生意。

sentences.en: You couldn't build some crazy, insane, super high revenue business.
sentences.zh: 你建不成那种疯狂、夸张、超高收入的生意。

sentences.en: You would eventually have to hire a team.
sentences.zh: 你最终不得不雇一个团队。

sentences.en: The thing there is that the bar has been raised as to how much you can make, because you can do more as one person with AI, but the barrier of entry to starting a one person business is now lower than ever.
sentences.zh: 关键在于，你能赚到的上限被拉高了，因为有了 AI，你一个人能做更多事，但启动一人企业的门槛现在比以往任何时候都低。

sentences.en: Anyone can do it right. You can ask AI.
sentences.zh: 谁都能干，对吧。你可以问 AI。

sentences.en: Hey, help me build a one person business.
sentences.zh: 嘿，帮我建一个一人企业。

sentences.en: Hey, this agent go and write content every day for me and spam every platform so anyone can try to build a one person business.
sentences.zh: 嘿，这个智能体去每天帮我写内容，去每个平台刷屏，所以任何人都可以尝试建一人企业。

sentences.en: Meaning there's more competition, but most people don't try beyond a certain point, 95 plus percent of people hit one failure and then quit altogether, and then the other people that don't want to learn, they download something like Opencore and buy a mac mini and start running all of these agents to do things for them.
sentences.zh: 这意味着竞争更激烈了，但大多数人过了某个点就不试了，95%以上的人遇到一次失败就直接放弃，然后另一群不想学的人，他们下载个像 Opencore 的东西，买台 Mac Mini，开始跑一堆智能体替他们干活。

sentences.en: But then you look at them two, three months from then and they have nothing to show for it.
sentences.zh: 但两三个月后你再去看他们，什么都拿不出来。

sentences.en: They just like looking at an agent doing things and they don't understand what quality is.
sentences.zh: 他们只是喜欢看着智能体做事，他们不懂什么叫质量。

sentences.en: They don't understand when something doesn't work, you change it.
sentences.zh: 他们不懂当某个东西不奏效时，你要去改它。

sentences.en: They don't understand that spamming every single platform, that doesn't mean you're going to grow on social media.
sentences.zh: 他们不懂在所有平台上刷屏，不代表你就能在社交媒体上增长。

sentences.en: That doesn't mean you're going to make any sales either.
sentences.zh: 也不代表你就能卖出任何东西。

sentences.en: When I actually talk to a few other of my business friends, some very high up in the business world, they try that stuff.
sentences.zh: 当我和几个做生意的朋友聊，有些在商业世界里位置很高，他们也试那些东西。

sentences.en: They try the open client. I'm not saying that it's bad at all.
sentences.zh: 他们试那个 open client。我不是说它不好。

sentences.en: We're actually introducing a very similar feature where you can chat with an agent on telegram into Eden, which is a software that we're building. It's in beta.
sentences.zh: 我们其实正在 Eden 里引入一个非常类似的功能，你可以通过 Telegram 跟智能体对话，Eden 是我们正在做的软件，目前在 beta 阶段。

sentences.en: You can sign up if you'd like, but what I'm saying is that most people just get a dopamine hit from it.
sentences.zh: 如果你愿意可以注册，但我想说的是，大多数人只是从中获得一次多巴胺快感。

sentences.en: They have this curve where it's like, oh, this is so awesome.
sentences.zh: 他们有一条曲线，就是那种"哇，这太牛了"。

sentences.en: I'm going to have it do everything they waste 203 hundred, $1,000 on AI credits, and then it collapses.
sentences.zh: 我要让它做所有事，他们在 AI 额度上浪费两三百、一千美元，然后它就崩了。

sentences.en: And then they have nothing because they don't know what good looks like.
sentences.zh: 然后他们一无所有，因为他们不知道"好"长什么样。

sentences.en: They don't have the skill or the knowledge to do the thing in the first place.
sentences.zh: 他们从一开始就没有做这件事的技能或知识。

sentences.en: So how are they going to be the manager or the CEO of the agents?
sentences.zh: 那他们怎么可能成为这些智能体的管理者或 CEO？

sentences.en: Now, with that rant out of the way, for the sake of this letter, we're going to set the goal of $1 million making $1 million with a one person business just so we can frame it. Right.
sentences.zh: 好了，吐槽到此为止，为了这封信的目的，我们把目标定在 100 万美元，用一人企业赚 100 万美元，只是为了有个框架，对吧。

sentences.en: I'm not saying you're going to make that.
sentences.zh: 我不是说你一定能赚到。

sentences.en: I'm not saying you're going to make anything.
sentences.zh: 我不是说你能赚到任何东西。

sentences.en: There's no amount of knowledge that I can just give you right now that will immediately make you $1 million.
sentences.zh: 我现在能直接给你的知识，没有任何一种能让你立刻赚到 100 万美元。

sentences.en: It doesn't work like that. Stop looking for videos like that.
sentences.zh: 不是那么回事。别再找那种视频了。

sentences.en: So we're just using the $1 million goal to make this tangible so we can actually break it down.
sentences.zh: 所以我们只是用 100 万美元这个目标让它变得具体，这样我们才能真正拆解它。

sentences.en: I'm going to share exactly what you need to learn how to use AI almost better than everyone else, and prompts that will give you that will allow you to really start your business today.
sentences.zh: 我会分享你到底需要学什么，才能把 AI 用得几乎比所有人都好，以及那些能让你今天真正启动你生意的提示词。

sentences.en: If you actually go through the prompts, which most people won't take the time to do that because it'll take about an hour to go through all of them, they're that comprehensive.
sentences.zh: 如果你真的把这些提示词过一遍——大多数人不会花这个时间，因为全部过完大概要一个小时，它们就是这么详尽。

sentences.en: Now, as a note, before we get started, we're not going over crazy agent workflows here.
sentences.zh: 先说一句，在我们开始之前，我们不会讲那些花里胡哨的智能体工作流。

sentences.en: We're just going over normal.
sentences.zh: 我们只讲最基础的。

sentences.en: I use and I know that sounds boring, but you need to learn the fundamentals before you can actually get into the crazy AI agent stuff, which we'll talk about in a future video if you like that, like comment, subscribe.
sentences.zh: 我用的是基础的东西，我知道这听起来很无聊，但你必须先学会基本功，才能真正去搞那些疯狂的 AI 智能体玩法——如果你们想看，点赞评论订阅，我们以后视频再聊。

sentences.en: So section one of this video, how do you actually make $1 million as one person?
sentences.zh: 那么本视频的第一部分：作为一个人，你到底怎么赚到 100 万美元？

sentences.en: Because to a lot of people, that just sounds insane.
sentences.zh: 因为对很多人来说，这听起来就是疯了。

sentences.en: And we need to break this down because you need to at least believe it's possible before you can do it.
sentences.zh: 我们必须把这个拆解清楚，因为你至少得先相信它是可能的，然后你才能做到。

sentences.en: And a lot of the people that don't believe it's possible will fall off of the video right now.
sentences.zh: 而那些不相信这可能的人，现在就会关掉这个视频。

sentences.en: So quick math. Let's do this.
sentences.zh: 来，快速算个账。

sentences.en: $1 million divided by 12 months is $83,333 per month.
sentences.zh: 100 万美元除以 12 个月，是每月 83,333 美元。

sentences.en: That number divided by 30 days is $2,777 per day.
sentences.zh: 这个数再除以 30 天，是每天 2,777 美元。

sentences.en: Now, there's a few ways to actually achieve that per day or per month.
sentences.zh: 那么，要实现这个每天或每月的目标，有几种方式。

sentences.en: You can sell 18 $150 products a day, like a course or whatever other product can cost $150.
sentences.zh: 你可以每天卖出 18 个 150 美元的产品，比如一门课程或者其他任何能定价 150 美元的产品。

sentences.en: You can sell 111 $25 subscriptions a day.
sentences.zh: 你可以每天卖出 111 个 25 美元的订阅。

sentences.en: So if you're starting on Substack, that's something you could do.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你在 Substack 上起步，这是你可以做的事。

sentences.en: Or you could go the freelance route and land a one $5,000 client every other day, which is a pretty high price point for just starting out and freelancing.
sentences.zh: 或者你可以走自由职业路线，每隔一天拿下一个 5,000 美元的客户——对于刚起步做自由职业来说，这个价位相当高了。

sentences.en: But it illustrates the point.
sentences.zh: 但它说明了核心逻辑。

sentences.en: If you go the coaching or consulting route or just service based business in general, you can land one $10,000 client every four days, or you can have a combination of both.
sentences.zh: 如果你走教练或咨询路线，或者任何服务型业务，你可以每四天拿下一个 10,000 美元的客户，或者你也可以两者结合。

sentences.en: So like 1 to 2 clients a week and a few other product or subscription sales a day, or just whatever other combination and price point there is to hit $1 million.
sentences.zh: 比如每周 1 到 2 个客户，再加上每天卖几个产品或订阅，或者其他任何能凑到 100 万美元的组合方式和价位。

sentences.en: Now, if you go the client route, I recommend doing that as a beginner because some people still don't believe this.
sentences.zh: 那么，如果你走客户路线，我建议初学者这么做，因为有些人到现在还是不信。

sentences.en: This was a limiting belief for myself as well.
sentences.zh: 我自己以前也有这个限制性信念。

sentences.en: It just feels weird charging such high prices, especially if you work.
sentences.zh: 收这么高的价格就是感觉很奇怪，尤其是如果你打过工。

sentences.en: When I worked at a web design agency, I was making like $60,000 a year, which isn't insanely good.
sentences.zh: 我在网页设计公司上班的时候，一年大概赚 6 万美元，不算特别好。

sentences.en: Is it insanely bad? It's not that great.
sentences.zh: 算特别差吗？也不算多好。

sentences.en: I was still living with four other people, paying a very low rent.
sentences.zh: 我当时还跟四个人合住，房租很低。

sentences.en: I still felt like I had money problems, even as like a single person at the time.
sentences.zh: 我依然觉得自己有金钱上的问题，即便那时候我还是单身。

sentences.en: But it's much easier to sell a 1000 to $5000 service to one person than it is to sell a 100 to 200 Substack subscriptions to 100 to 200 people.
sentences.zh: 但卖一个 1,000 到 5,000 美元的服务给一个人，比卖 100 到 200 个 Substack 订阅给 100 到 200 个人要容易得多。

sentences.en: Because where are you going to find those people?
sentences.zh: 因为你去哪找那些人？

sentences.en: And how are you going to convince them?
sentences.zh: 你又怎么说服他们？

sentences.en: That's what the social media audience is for or other traffic mechanisms.
sentences.zh: 这就是社交媒体受众或者其他流量机制的作用。

sentences.en: But you absolutely can send 100 DMs today.
sentences.zh: 但你今天绝对可以发出 100 条私信。

sentences.en: Ask AI how to send a good DM and if you have a decent offer that people want, they may be willing to pay you.
sentences.zh: 问问 AI 怎么写一条好的私信，如果你有一个人们想要的、还不错的 offer，他们可能愿意付钱给你。

sentences.en: And if you aren't a business owner, you may not understand that yet because you don't understand that businesses want to grow.
sentences.zh: 如果你不是一个企业主，你可能还不理解这一点，因为你不理解企业想要增长。

sentences.en: And if you can help them grow or make more money, they're going to want to pay you.
sentences.zh: 而如果你能帮他们增长或赚更多钱，他们就会想付钱给你。

sentences.en: The amount of people that I have hired for 1000, 5000, 10,000, $50,000 after starting a business is absurd.
sentences.zh: 我创业之后雇过的人，金额从1000美元、5000美元、1万美元到5万美元都有，数量多到离谱。

sentences.en: But if the ROI is there, the ROI is there.
sentences.zh: 但只要ROI成立，它就是成立。

sentences.en: So as a beginner, you don't really have an audience yet, and you may not be building one.
sentences.zh: 作为新手，你目前还没有什么受众，你可能也没在构建受众。

sentences.en: But that's what I recommend doing as well, because that's also going to prove that you know what you're talking about.
sentences.zh: 但我还是建议你去做这件事，因为这也能证明你真的懂你在说什么。

sentences.en: When you reach out to clients, they're probably going to look at your social media profiles.
sentences.zh: 当你去联系客户的时候，他们很可能会去看你的社交媒体主页。

sentences.en: And building an audience is leverage.
sentences.zh: 而构建受众本身就是杠杆。

sentences.en: So why wouldn't you do that? Why wouldn't you write content?
sentences.zh: 那你为什么不做呢？为什么不写内容呢？

sentences.en: And once you're writing content, once you're actually growing, then if you want to transition out of client work into something like a product that can sell while you sleep, so to say, based on the traffic that you generate, then you'd go to the product route.
sentences.zh: 一旦你开始写内容，一旦你真的在增长，然后如果你想从客户工作转向产品路线——那种能靠你产生的流量在你睡觉时自动销售的产品——那你就可以走产品路线了。

sentences.en: So the question there with the product route, because that's usually most people's goal, is like, I don't want to do client work.
sentences.zh: 产品路线这里的问题在于——因为这通常是大多数人的目标——就是"我不想做客户工作"。

sentences.en: I didn't I hated client work, but it was a necessary step for me.
sentences.zh: 我也不喜欢客户工作，我讨厌它，但它对我来说是必经的一步。

sentences.en: But when you go the product route, how do you actually get enough traffic to the product so that you can make that many sales to make $1 million?
sentences.zh: 但当你走产品路线的时候，你到底怎么给产品带来足够多的流量，才能卖出那么多单、做到100万美元？

sentences.en: So let's do more math at a 2.5% conversion rate on a landing page, meaning 2.5% of the people that go to the landing page actually buy the thing that you're selling.
sentences.zh: 那我们再算一下：按着陆页2.5%的转化率来算，也就是说，访问着陆页的人里有2.5%会真正购买你卖的东西。

sentences.en: You need about 720 people to visit that page a day, to make 18 sales on a $150 product, or you need something like a post to go viral once or twice a month, which I wouldn't bet on, but is becoming more and more of a thing as the social media platforms are becoming more interest algorithm related, right?
sentences.zh: 你需要每天大约720人访问那个页面，才能在150美元的产品上产生18笔销售；或者你需要一篇帖子每个月爆一两次——我不会押注在这上面，但随着社交媒体平台越来越偏向兴趣算法，这种情况确实越来越常见了，对吧？

sentences.en: Really? Anyone?
sentences.zh: 真的，任何人都可以。

sentences.en: Even if you're just starting off, if you can create good content, you can post your first reel, it'll go mega viral.
sentences.zh: 就算你刚起步，如果你能做出好内容，你发第一条Reel就可能超级爆。

sentences.en: But most people don't know how to create content, so that's usually not going to happen unless it's based on luck.
sentences.zh: 但大多数人根本不知道怎么创作内容，所以除非靠运气，否则通常不会发生。

sentences.en: So the bit that I like to take is continuously building an audience, putting out content, iterating, refining, and improving your skill over time so that your audience growth kind of reflects the growth of your skill.
sentences.zh: 所以我喜欢走的路子是：持续构建受众、持续输出内容、不断迭代、打磨、随着时间提升你的技能，让你的受众增长大致反映出你技能的增长。

sentences.en: So getting 720 people to a landing page a day to make $1 million, where does that actually come from?
sentences.zh: 那么，每天让720人访问着陆页、做到100万美元，这些流量到底从哪里来？

sentences.en: It can come from social media.
sentences.zh: 可以来自社交媒体。

sentences.en: It can come from ads like Facebook ads or Google ads.
sentences.zh: 可以来自广告，比如Facebook广告或Google广告。

sentences.en: It can come from SEO.
sentences.zh: 可以来自SEO。

sentences.en: It can come from influencer partnerships.
sentences.zh: 可以来自网红合作。

sentences.en: It can come from podcast sponsorships, newsletters, sponsorships.
sentences.zh: 可以来自播客赞助、Newsletter赞助。

sentences.en: It can really come from anything.
sentences.zh: 真的可以来自任何地方。

sentences.en: But you are one person.
sentences.zh: 但你只是一个人。

sentences.en: And if you're like I was when I first started out, you don't have that much money and you don't want to spend that much money.
sentences.zh: 而且如果你像我刚起步时那样，你没那么多钱，你也不想花那么多钱。

sentences.en: So what are you going to do?
sentences.zh: 那你怎么办？

sentences.en: You're going to do social media and you're going to get really good at capturing attention, delivering value, delivering substance, not just copying templates, not just following the trends, but getting very good at what you do.
sentences.zh: 你就做社交媒体，你要变得非常擅长抓住注意力、交付价值、交付实质内容，不只是复制模板，不只是追热点，而是把你做的事情做到非常出色。

sentences.en: And showing other people that you're good at what you do.
sentences.zh: 并且让别人看到你擅长你所做的事。

sentences.en: So if we assume that you start on social media, you start writing content and you become skilled at that thing and you continue to refine your skill, that means you're not stagnating.
sentences.zh: 所以假设你从社交媒体起步，你开始写内容，你在这件事上变得熟练，并且持续打磨你的技能，这意味着你没有停滞。

sentences.en: You're constantly learning.
sentences.zh: 你在持续学习。

sentences.en: It's actually a baked in portion of your day of studying other people's content, implementing what you learn in your own, and improving over time.
sentences.zh: 这实际上是你一天中内嵌的一部分：研究别人的内容，把你学到的东西应用到自己的内容里，然后随着时间不断进步。

sentences.en: Because social media, yes, it's a skill.
sentences.zh: 因为社交媒体，是的，它是一门技能。

sentences.en: It's not completely based on luck.
sentences.zh: 它不完全基于运气。

sentences.en: It's partially based on luck for actually growing, like getting the traction started.
sentences.zh: 能不能真正做起来、获得初始增长，确实有一部分靠运气。

sentences.en: Once you have a base audience, then you have a base level of engagement and you're more likely to go viral over time.
sentences.zh: 一旦你有了基础受众，有了基础互动量，随着时间推移，你走红的概率就会越来越大。

sentences.en: So you have to get through that beginner hell, but you absolutely can.
sentences.zh: 所以你必须熬过新手地狱，但你绝对能熬过去。

sentences.en: So if you become skilled at it, then you can get 10 to 50,000 views per YouTube video, and you can also get 500,000 to 1 million impressions on social media per month.
sentences.zh: 一旦你把这门技能练熟了，每条 YouTube 视频能拿到 1 万到 5 万播放，社交媒体上每月也能拿到 50 万到 100 万次曝光。

sentences.en: And yes, it will take some time to do that.
sentences.zh: 当然，做到这一步需要一些时间。

sentences.en: If you're not immediately good at the thing, shocker.
sentences.zh: 如果你不是一上来就擅长这件事——很震惊吧。

sentences.en: You actually have to get good at something in order to see results. Crazy.
sentences.zh: 你确实得先把一件事做好，才能看到结果。很疯狂对吧。

sentences.en: You can't just go to a school, get a degree in social media, and immediately have 50,000 followers.
sentences.zh: 你不可能去上个学、拿个社交媒体学位，然后立刻就有 5 万粉丝。

sentences.en: No, this is based on real world feedback.
sentences.zh: 不可能，这是基于真实世界的反馈。

sentences.en: This is based on skill.
sentences.zh: 这是基于技能。

sentences.en: But the thing there is, is even if you don't get 10 to 50,000 YouTube views, or 500,000 to 1 million impressions, even less than that.
sentences.zh: 但关键在于，就算你拿不到 1 万到 5 万的 YouTube 播放，或者 50 万到 100 万次曝光，哪怕比这个少。

sentences.en: It's not like you're making $0 if you actually do this stuff.
sentences.zh: 只要你真的去做这些事，你也不会是零收入。

sentences.en: Many people would be very happy with less than $1 million per year.
sentences.zh: 很多人一年赚不到 100 万美元也会很开心。

sentences.en: So if you think about it, you need 720 people a day to the landing page.
sentences.zh: 所以你想一想，你每天需要 720 个人访问落地页。

sentences.en: And if you're getting that many impressions, 720 people is a challenge for sure.
sentences.zh: 如果你能拿到那么多曝光，720 个人确实是个挑战。

sentences.en: But it's not too much to ask for.
sentences.zh: 但并不是一个过分的要求。

sentences.en: Now, the objections in your mind that are probably happening right now is like, oh, I can't do this.
sentences.zh: 现在，你脑子里可能正在冒出来的反对声音是：哦，我做不到。

sentences.en: So this sounds unfeasible.
sentences.zh: 所以这听起来不可行。

sentences.en: It's because you're probably stuck in the old paradigm.
sentences.zh: 那是因为你可能还困在旧的思维模式里。

sentences.en: You're stuck in the my time equals how much I earn rather than my how much I earn equals the value that I provide.
sentences.zh: 你困在“我的时间等于我赚多少钱”，而不是“我赚多少钱等于我提供了多少价值”。

sentences.en: If the only life you've known is go to school and get a job, then you are.
sentences.zh: 如果你这辈子只知道上学、找工作，那你就是这样。

sentences.en: That is your mindset.
sentences.zh: 那就是你的思维模式。

sentences.en: That's what you are wired to believe.
sentences.zh: 那就是你被设定去相信的东西。

sentences.en: That's what you're wired to do.
sentences.zh: 那就是你被设定去做的事。

sentences.en: If you want to make more money, you have to get a better job or you have to get better schooling.
sentences.zh: 如果你想赚更多钱，你就得找一份更好的工作，或者去读更好的学校。

sentences.en: You don't understand that if you're an entrepreneur, you hunt for your better job.
sentences.zh: 你不理解，如果你是一个创业者，你是自己去猎取更好的工作。

sentences.en: You hunt for your gigs, you hunt, hunt for your customers, and you self educate.
sentences.zh: 你自己去猎取项目，自己去猎取客户，自己教育自己。

sentences.en: You don't need to go to an institution to get a credential in order for someone to hire you.
sentences.zh: 你不需要去一个机构拿一张证书，然后等着别人来雇你。

sentences.en: It's all in your own hands.
sentences.zh: 一切都在你自己手里。

sentences.en: And that's a great thing for many people who actually want that.
sentences.zh: 对于真正想要这种生活的人来说，这是一件大好事。

sentences.en: But a lot of people aren't willing to deal with the uncertainty that comes with that.
sentences.zh: 但很多人不愿意面对随之而来的不确定性。

sentences.en: So that's another skill that you have to learn is just tolerating and mitigating the risk of starting a business.
sentences.zh: 所以这是你必须学会的另一项技能：容忍并降低创业的风险。

sentences.en: So to actually get started on this stuff, it takes about 2 to 5 years to get really good at those things, at branding, at content and marketing, at sales, at all of these things.
sentences.zh: 所以真正开始做这些事，大概需要 2 到 5 年才能变得非常擅长——品牌、内容和营销、销售，所有这些。

sentences.en: But with AI, if we train them on the principles of experts who willingly put out their knowledge on the internet like Alex or Mozi, sales expert, marketing expert, you have so many different people that talk about branding, about content, so on and so forth.
sentences.zh: 但有了 AI，如果我们用那些专家的原则来训练它，那些愿意把自己的知识公开放在互联网上的人，比如 Alex Hormozi、销售专家、营销专家，有那么多人在讲品牌、讲内容，等等。

sentences.en: Why can't you take that knowledge and then have the AI help you through that process?
sentences.zh: 你为什么不能把这些知识拿过来，让AI帮你走完这个过程？

sentences.en: And that's kind of what we're going to do for the first step, when we actually use AI.
sentences.zh: 这差不多就是我们第一步要做的事，真正开始用AI的时候。

sentences.en: So let's actually get into it.
sentences.zh: 那我们直接开始吧。

sentences.en: How do you actually build the one person business with AI and what's the entire workflow?
sentences.zh: 到底怎么用AI打造一人企业？整个工作流程是什么样的？

sentences.en: So as you know by now, the core difference between starting a one person business a few years ago and now is just AI, an entire course can fit into a prompt.
sentences.zh: 到现在你应该知道了，几年前创办一人企业和现在的核心区别就是AI，一整门课程可以浓缩进一个提示词里。

sentences.en: And if a prompt helps you actually do the thing, then that's like a course on steroids because you're actually getting results potentially.
sentences.zh: 如果一个提示词能帮你真正把事情做了，那它就像一门打了激素的课程，因为你真的有可能拿到结果。

sentences.en: So for this specifically, we're going to go over a canvas template, a canvas is a feature in Eden that we polished up.
sentences.zh: 具体来说，我们会讲一个画布模板，画布是Eden里我们打磨过的一个功能。

sentences.en: We've made pretty freaking good at this point.
sentences.zh: 现在做得相当不错了。

sentences.en: And this is where I do like my weekly writing. Right?
sentences.zh: 我就是在这里做每周写作的，对吧？

sentences.en: So every week I create a canvas, I paste tweets on there, I paste YouTube videos that inspired me.
sentences.zh: 每周我创建一个画布，把推文贴上去，把启发我的YouTube视频贴上去。

sentences.en: I put a markdown document for my outline for my newsletter.
sentences.zh: 我放一个markdown文档，写我的newsletter大纲。

sentences.en: I put my prompts on there for like social posts and for title generation, for YouTube and for B-roll ideas.
sentences.zh: 我把提示词放上去，用来生成社交媒体帖子和标题，给YouTube用的，还有B-roll创意。

sentences.en: And then I connect things to I chat to stress test ideas or just talk to the specific content.
sentences.zh: 然后我把内容连接到AI聊天，用来压力测试想法，或者直接跟特定内容对话。

sentences.en: Like if I watch a YouTube video that week and I knew an idea was in there, then I talk to it.
sentences.zh: 比如那周我看了一个YouTube视频，知道里面有个想法，我就跟它聊。

sentences.en: Then I'd go to my newsletter, open that, and start writing again.
sentences.zh: 然后我去打开我的newsletter，继续写。

sentences.en: But we're going to use an entire one person business canvas, and you can duplicate the template in the description with the link.
sentences.zh: 但我们要用的是一整个一人企业画布，你可以用描述里的链接复制这个模板。

sentences.en: And I'd highly recommend working through this on a desktop, because that's where you're going to do work and you're not going to be distracted and canvas apps in general just aren't very good on mobile.
sentences.zh: 我强烈建议在电脑上完成这个过程，因为那是你真正工作的地方，你不会分心，而且画布类应用在手机上普遍不太好用。

sentences.en: So if you save the link on your phone and then go back to it on desktop, and then you can save all of those files duplicated, because Eden is also a drive in a workspace.
sentences.zh: 所以你可以在手机上保存链接，然后回到电脑上打开，这样你就可以保存所有复制出来的文件，因为Eden同时也是一个云端硬盘和工作空间。

sentences.en: So you can write.
sentences.zh: 所以你可以写作。

sentences.en: It's not just a canvas.
sentences.zh: 它不只是一个画布。

sentences.en: Anything you upload, including YouTube videos, regular videos.
sentences.zh: 你上传的任何东西，包括YouTube视频、普通视频。

sentences.en: We analyze all of the frames for you so you can search for each frame, transcript, match, so on and so forth.
sentences.zh: 我们会帮你分析所有帧，这样你可以搜索每一帧、转录文本、匹配内容等等。

sentences.en: It's pretty cool, but if you follow the template exactly, you will have the three pillars of a modern, successful one person business or if it's not immediately successful, which it probably won't be, don't expect that you have a starting point that you can actually start doing things, and it's not a guessing game anymore.
sentences.zh: 挺酷的，但如果你完全按照模板来做，你就会拥有一个现代、成功的一人企业的三大支柱——就算不是立刻成功，大概率也不会立刻成功，别抱这种期待——你会有一个真正的起点，可以开始做事了，不再是瞎猜。

sentences.en: And those three pillars that you'll have are one.
sentences.zh: 你将拥有的三大支柱是：第一。

sentences.en: A brand, which is who you are, what you help people achieve, and why people should care about both. Two is content.
sentences.zh: 品牌，也就是你是谁、你帮人们实现什么、以及人们为什么应该关心这两点。第二是内容。

sentences.en: So your ideas, opinions and teachings that attract people to your brand three is offer so your product, service and compelling landing page you can send people to from your content.
sentences.zh: 也就是你的想法、观点和教导，用来吸引人们关注你的品牌。第三是产品，也就是你的产品、服务和有说服力的落地页，你可以从内容把人引导过去。

sentences.en: Now I want this to be a bit educational as well.
sentences.zh: 我想让这个内容也带点教育性质。

sentences.en: So we're going to go through each of these pillars brand content and offer what you sell just so you understand the importance of these things.
sentences.zh: 所以我们会逐一讲这三大支柱——品牌、内容和产品，也就是你卖什么——让你理解这些东西的重要性。

sentences.en: So inside of the template, one, there's an entire video here that you can click and watch.
sentences.zh: 在模板里面，第一，这里有一个完整的视频，你可以点击观看。

sentences.en: And I go over how to use the entire template.
sentences.zh: 我会讲怎么使用整个模板。

sentences.en: But the first thing we're starting with is just a personal brand strategy.
sentences.zh: 但我们首先要开始的，就是个人品牌策略。

sentences.en: And what I have here.
sentences.zh: 我这里有——

sentences.en: Oh, you can see another person on here because the template is shared, but you can see that there's a prompt here connected to an AI chat.
sentences.zh: 哦，你能看到另一个人也在上面，因为模板是共享的，但你可以看到这里有一个提示词，连接到一个AI聊天。

sentences.en: I can full screen this AI chat or I can just zoom into it and start typing here.
sentences.zh: 我可以全屏这个AI聊天，也可以直接放大它，在这里开始打字。

sentences.en: But we'll talk about what's actually in here.
sentences.zh: 但我们先聊聊这里面到底有什么。

sentences.en: But if you also want to consult with experts, I've curated three videos and these are all connected to this chat so I can chat in here to refine my personal brand strategy, ask questions about personal branding, so on and so forth.
sentences.zh: 如果你想咨询专家，我精选了三个视频，它们都关联到这个聊天窗口，我可以在这里聊天来打磨我的个人品牌策略、问关于个人品牌的问题，等等。

sentences.en: And you can also paste video links or just upload your own knowledge inside of this section.
sentences.zh: 你也可以在这个区域粘贴视频链接，或者上传你自己的知识。

sentences.en: But as one person on social media, you're starting a personal brand.
sentences.zh: 作为社交媒体上的一个人，你正在启动一个个人品牌。

sentences.en: That's what you're doing. Why are you doing that?
sentences.zh: 这就是你在做的事。为什么要做这件事？

sentences.en: Because if you want to make money, you need something to sell and people to actually see and buy that thing.
sentences.zh: 因为如果你想赚钱，你需要有东西可卖，也需要有人真的看到并购买那个东西。

sentences.en: A personal brand is neither of those things, but you can think of it as a sort of digital storefront or a digital resume.
sentences.zh: 个人品牌不是这两者中的任何一个，但你可以把它想象成一个数字店面，或者一份数字简历。

sentences.en: It's a layer of trust between those two things.
sentences.zh: 它是横在这两者之间的一层信任。

sentences.en: It's where your content goes under because you post via a personal brand, and then inside of your content, you promote your product or service.
sentences.zh: 你的内容从它这里经过——因为你通过个人品牌发布内容，然后在内容里推广你的产品或服务。

sentences.en: And since people follow your personal brand and hopefully they like your personal brand, then they're more likely to be receptive to your content and purchase your product or service.
sentences.zh: 而既然人们关注了你的个人品牌，并且希望他们喜欢你的个人品牌，那他们就更有可能接受你的内容，并购买你的产品或服务。

sentences.en: And in the age of AI, when content is just, it can be endless and it's going to be flooding social media.
sentences.zh: 在 AI 时代，当内容可以无穷无尽，并且即将淹没社交媒体的时候。

sentences.en: What are people going to turn to?
sentences.zh: 人们会转向什么？

sentences.en: They're going to turn to who they trust.
sentences.zh: 他们会转向他们信任的人。

sentences.en: Who is that?
sentences.zh: 那是谁？

sentences.en: A personal brand who they can almost verify is a human, and they can tell whether or not they're using AI in a non tasteful way.
sentences.zh: 一个他们几乎能验证是人类的个人品牌，他们能判断你是否在用一种没品位的方式使用 AI。

sentences.en: And another thing here is I don't care about how cringe you think the word personal brand is.
sentences.zh: 还有一点，我不在乎你觉得"个人品牌"这个词有多尬。

sentences.en: I understand that every space has gotten flooded with it and all you have to use these templates, you have to use this strategy.
sentences.zh: 我理解每个领域都被它淹没了，什么你必须用这些模板，你必须用这套策略。

sentences.en: Here's how you grow to a million followers in zero days.
sentences.zh: 什么零天涨到百万粉丝。

sentences.en: But that's what you're doing when you're one person on social media. So get over it.
sentences.zh: 但当你是社交媒体上的一个人时，这就是你在做的事。所以别纠结了。

sentences.en: If it helps you to think of a personal brand as just like a vessel for your life's work or a way to do something meaningful, or if you just want to think of yourself as a person on social media and not a brand, then go ahead and do that.
sentences.zh: 如果把它想成你毕生事业的载体、或者一种做有意义事情的方式能帮到你，或者你只想把自己当成社交媒体上的一个人而不是一个品牌，那就这么去做。

sentences.en: And now we've discussed my actual personal brand strategy and what I recommend in many other videos.
sentences.zh: 现在我们已经讨论了我实际的个人品牌策略，以及我在很多其他视频里推荐的东西。

sentences.en: So we're going to keep this brief.
sentences.zh: 所以我们长话短说。

sentences.en: This is my recommended strategy, not the only strategy or one that you have to follow.
sentences.zh: 这是我推荐的策略，不是唯一的策略，也不是你必须遵循的策略。

sentences.en: For social media.
sentences.zh: 针对社交媒体。

sentences.en: The first principle is that you are the niche your beliefs, experiences, and interests give you a unique point of view that reflects in your content and products.
sentences.zh: 原则一：你自己就是细分领域。你的信念、经历和兴趣给了你一个独特的视角，它会反映在你的内容和产品里。

sentences.en: Principle two is that you need a few content pillars.
sentences.zh: 原则二：你需要几个内容支柱。

sentences.en: You need one skill or interest you plan to monetize as a topic, and then two complementary interests that you can't shut up about as complementary topics.
sentences.zh: 你需要一个你打算变现的技能或兴趣作为主题，再加上两个你聊起来就停不下来的互补兴趣，作为互补主题。

sentences.en: Principle three is that you need to ground those content pillars in pain points.
sentences.zh: 原则三：你需要把这些内容支柱扎根在痛点里。

sentences.en: Foundational content topics, and high performing ideas.
sentences.zh: 基础内容主题，以及高表现力的想法。

sentences.en: This is where most people mess up is they're like, okay, I like these topics.
sentences.zh: 大多数人搞砸的地方就在这里——他们觉得，好，我喜欢这些主题。

sentences.en: I have this idea, I'm just going to write about it, but they don't pay attention to why it's important to the actual person.
sentences.zh: 我有这个想法，我直接写就行了，但他们不去关注这对屏幕另一边那个真实的人来说为什么重要。

sentences.en: On the other side of the screen.
sentences.zh: 对屏幕另一边那个人。

sentences.en: They write this freely tweet, and they think they're Marcus Aurelius, but you don't have the reputational authority that Marcus Aurelius has.
sentences.zh: 他们写了一条自由发挥的推文，就觉得自己是马可·奥勒留，但你没有马可·奥勒留那种声誉权威。

sentences.en: You're not Alan Watts, you're not these people who have this reputation built up so that anything they say is valuable.
sentences.zh: 你不是 Alan Watts，你不是那些已经建立起声誉的人，所以他们说什么都有价值。

sentences.en: You have to practice persuasion.
sentences.zh: 你得练习说服力。

sentences.en: You have to capture attention.
sentences.zh: 你得学会抓注意力。

sentences.en: You have to illustrate, hey, why is this idea important for my life?
sentences.zh: 你得讲清楚——嘿，这个想法为什么对我的人生很重要？

sentences.en: And that usually comes in the form of a pain point.
sentences.zh: 这通常会以痛点的形式出现。

sentences.en: So helping people understand why they should implement the idea.
sentences.zh: 就是帮别人理解，为什么他们应该把这个想法用起来。

sentences.en: Foundational content topics are just those that are like evergreen.
sentences.zh: 基础型内容选题，就是那些常青的、永远不过时的。

sentences.en: They're the ones that, you know, work.
sentences.zh: 就是那些，你知道，确实有效的选题。

sentences.en: They're the ones that you see everywhere, and you should probably implement under your own brand in your own voice, because they just work.
sentences.zh: 就是那些你到处都能看到的选题，而你应该用自己的品牌、自己的声音去做，因为它们就是管用。

sentences.en: And then high performing topics are the outliers that tend to do very well.
sentences.zh: 然后是爆款型选题，就是那些表现远超平均的异类。

sentences.en: When you go on YouTube and you see a video that's just doing so much better than everyone else's videos, or even that person's own videos, that's an outlier.
sentences.zh: 当你在 YouTube 上看到一个视频，表现远远好过其他人的视频，甚至远超那个人自己的其他视频，这就是一个异类。

sentences.en: That's a signal that you should probably take note of that and put it in your swipe file and eat and paste the YouTube link in Eden, and we download it, transcribe it, so on and so forth, so that you can talk with it with AI or the entire folder of your swipe file or all of the images that you've saved.
sentences.zh: 这是一个信号，你应该把它记下来，放进你的素材库，把 YouTube 链接粘贴到 Eden 里，我们下载它、转录它，等等等等，这样你就可以用 AI 跟它对话，或者跟整个素材库文件夹、跟你保存的所有图片对话。

sentences.en: So on and so forth. Eden's very cool.
sentences.zh: 等等等等。Eden 真的很酷。

sentences.en: Please catch on and use it already.
sentences.zh: 赶紧跟上，用起来吧。

sentences.en: But you save those and then you take your own ideas and you start to like reformulate them so that they work better.
sentences.zh: 你把这些存下来，然后拿出你自己的想法，开始重新组合它们，让它们效果更好。

sentences.en: Now, principle four is that you need to turn all of that into a 1 to 2 sentence social media bio that gets across the most attractive parts.
sentences.zh: 好，原则四：你需要把以上所有东西，浓缩成一句到两句的社交媒体简介，传达出最吸引人的部分。

sentences.en: I'm not going to go over a social media bio format, but if you go through the personal brand strategy prompt in the canvas here, then it will help do that for you.
sentences.zh: 我不打算展开讲简介的格式，但如果你用画布里的个人品牌策略提示词走一遍，它会帮你搞定。

sentences.en: And after you finish this, it'll interview you for a decent amount of time, and then it will spit out the actual personal brand strategy that you can save in your workspace in a folder or in other places, and you can refer to often another thing you can do in the near future when we have the open class slash telegram agent, this is only on my branch.
sentences.zh: 你走完之后，它会花不少时间采访你，然后直接输出一份真正的个人品牌策略，你可以保存在工作区的文件夹里或者其他地方，经常拿出来参考。另一件你不久之后可以做的事——等我们有了开放课程/Telegram 智能体，这个目前只在我的分支上。

sentences.en: This looks a lot more styled and better, but you can send this to telegram and then you can just have the AI bounce ideas back and forth with you, or have it actually do things like access your Twitter and post content or schedule content.
sentences.zh: 这个版本样式好看很多，你可以把它发到 Telegram，然后让 AI 跟你来回碰撞想法，或者让它真的去做事，比如访问你的 Twitter、发布内容或排期内容。

sentences.en: So inside of the canvas and outside of the canvas, how do you actually use AI to create a personal brand better?
sentences.zh: 那么在画布之内和画布之外，你到底怎么用 AI 更好地打造个人品牌？

sentences.en: The first thing is you can curate expert information and have a conversation with it.
sentences.zh: 第一件事，你可以精选专家信息，然后跟它对话。

sentences.en: As an example, you could find YouTube videos or books from people who are certified experts and add those to a chat, rather than asking for a general AI opinion.
sentences.zh: 举个例子，你可以找那些有认证的专家的 YouTube 视频或书籍，把它们加进对话里，而不是直接问 AI 要一个泛泛的意见。

sentences.en: Because I works best when you know what you want, that's really the simplest one.
sentences.zh: 因为当你知道自己想要什么的时候，效果最好，这真的是最简单的一条。

sentences.en: And then, as I've talked about before, the second and more complex one is to take that expert information, break it down into a simplified guide that you'll be able to give to the AI.
sentences.zh: 然后，我之前也讲过，第二件更复杂的事，是把那些专家信息拆解成一个简化版指南，让你能够交给 AI。

sentences.en: It's like I can take a piece of content, or I can take this guy's personal brand strategy, and then I can ask AI to turn it into a guide.
sentences.zh: 就像我可以拿一篇内容，或者拿某个人的个人品牌策略，然后让 AI 把它变成一个指南。

sentences.en: So it removes all of the fluff from that, and then you can turn that into whatever kind of prompt you want.
sentences.zh: 这样就去掉了所有水分，然后你可以把它变成任何你想要的提示词。

sentences.en: That's what I did for the prompt on the canvas, but I did it with my own personal brand strategy.
sentences.zh: 我就是这么为画布上的提示词做的，只不过我用的是我自己的个人品牌策略。

sentences.en: Now, the type of prompt that you can create is spitting out a blueprint or acting as a coach.
sentences.zh: 那么，你可以创建的提示词类型，是输出蓝图，或者扮演一个教练。

sentences.en: I could say, hey, take this guide and let's turn it into a prompt that first ask for information from me so that it knows what kind of personal brand I actually want to create.
sentences.zh: 我可以说，嘿，拿着这个指南，我们把它变成一个提示词，先向我收集信息，让它知道我到底想打造什么样的个人品牌。

sentences.en: And then after that context gathering phase and interview phase, just coach me day by day into doing this.
sentences.zh: 然后，在信息收集和采访阶段之后，就一天一天地指导我去执行。

sentences.en: Make sure I write content, make sure I have my bio set up, make sure I report back to you, so on and so forth.
sentences.zh: 确保我写内容，确保我设好简介，确保我向你汇报，等等等等。

sentences.en: You can just turn it into a coach or another person that holds you accountable.
sentences.zh: 你可以直接把它变成一个教练，或者另一个能让你对自己负责的人。

sentences.en: And if you do this inside of something like an agent or custom agent in Eden, when that's ready, you can set a specific schedule for this to happen so it can send you a prompt like you can send a prompt at a certain time so that, let's say it reaches out to you to give you a source of inspiration and tell you to turn that into a post that you then refine with it, and then it can post directly to Twitter.
sentences.zh: 如果你在类似 Eden 里的智能体或自定义智能体里做这件事——等它准备好了——你可以设定一个具体的时间表，让它按计划执行，比如在某个时间给你发一条提示，主动联系你，给你一个灵感来源，让你把它变成一篇帖子，你跟它一起打磨，然后它可以直接发到 Twitter。

sentences.en: So that's a more tasteful way of using AI rather than just saying, hey, go and write all this shit content for me, and I'll probably go over that in a future video or newsletter.
sentences.zh: 这是一种更有品味的 AI 用法，而不是简单地说，嘿，去给我写一堆垃圾内容。这个我可能会在以后的视频或 newsletter 里展开讲。

sentences.en: So subscribe to my Substack if you want to get that.
sentences.zh: 所以想收到的话，订阅我的 Substack。

sentences.en: So that's starting a personal brand.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是从个人品牌起步。

sentences.en: Go through the prompt, refine it, study it.
sentences.zh: 把提示词过一遍，打磨它，研究它。

sentences.en: The second thing is, how do you actually write content that is better than most beginners?
sentences.zh: 第二件事是，你怎么写出比大多数新手更好的内容？

sentences.en: How do you stand out?
sentences.zh: 你怎么脱颖而出？

sentences.en: I've been doing this for a while.
sentences.zh: 我干这行有段时间了。

sentences.en: I've been writing content for maybe 6 to 7 years now.
sentences.zh: 我写内容大概六七年了。

sentences.en: I can read a tweet or look at a YouTube title or watch a YouTube video, or read an article, and I can know whether or not it's going to do well just because my, like, pattern recognition has gotten to that point.
sentences.zh: 我现在看一条推文、一个 YouTube 标题、一个 YouTube 视频，或者一篇文章，就能判断它会不会火，因为我的模式识别能力已经练到了那个程度。

sentences.en: And we've talked about this before, but the biggest problem beginners make is not illustrating the importance of the idea they are trying to convey.
sentences.zh: 我们之前聊过这个，但新手最大的问题是，他们没有把想传达的那个想法的重要性讲清楚。

sentences.en: They have interesting ideas, but they can't make it interesting to other people now in order to make an idea interesting to someone else, you need to provide a compelling why.
sentences.zh: 他们有有趣的想法，但没法让别人也觉得有趣。要让别人觉得一个想法有趣，你得给出一个让人信服的理由。

sentences.en: You need to give them a reason to change their behavior.
sentences.zh: 你得给他们一个改变行为的理由。

sentences.en: Because if you're the one who changes their behavior, they will remember you as the person who, quote unquote, changed their life, and they will start to trust you over any human or AI.
sentences.zh: 因为如果是你改变了他们的行为，他们会记住你，把你当成那个"改变了自己人生"的人，然后他们会开始信任你，超过信任任何人类或 AI。

sentences.en: In other words, the secret to writing content is to one have a good idea, and two, have a pain point it solves or a benefit it gives.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，写内容的秘诀就是：第一，有一个好想法；第二，有一个它能解决的痛点，或者它能带来的好处。

sentences.en: And you need to illustrate that reason well, the best way to understand this, or to just do this in general, is if you're reading something and you have an idea or you're reflecting on your life and you have an idea that you know you want to post, right, that's kind of how creators act is they are just constantly turning ideas into something that they can post.
sentences.zh: 而且你得把这个理由讲好。理解这一点、或者说直接上手做这件事，最好的方式就是：当你在读东西时冒出一个想法，或者在反思人生时冒出一个想法，你知道自己想发出去——创作者就是这么运作的，他们就是不断把想法变成可以发出去的东西。

sentences.en: It's just automatic for them to have an idea and immediately write it down.
sentences.zh: 对他们来说，冒出一个想法然后立刻写下来，已经是自动反应了。

sentences.en: But what you do during that step as well is think of what's a pain point or a benefit of this that helps other people or that people actually want, and then you have to bake that into the idea.
sentences.zh: 但你在这一步还要做的是，想一想：这个想法有什么痛点或好处，能帮到别人、或者别人真的想要？然后你得把这个融进想法里。

sentences.en: Now, the second mistake that beginners make is that they just don't understand how everything fits together.
sentences.zh: 好，新手犯的第二个错误是，他们就是搞不懂所有东西是怎么拼在一起的。

sentences.en: They get good at writing content or creating reels on social media, but they feel like it's pointless because they don't know how to make money from it.
sentences.zh: 他们变得擅长写内容、或者在社交媒体上做 Reels，但他们觉得这没什么意义，因为他们不知道怎么从中赚钱。

sentences.en: So at that point, they start catering to the algorithm or just having I do everything for them just so they can get the dopamine hit of likes and engagement.
sentences.zh: 到了这个阶段，他们就开始迎合算法，或者干脆让 AI 包办一切，只为了从点赞和互动里获得那点多巴胺快感。

sentences.en: But still they don't know how to monetize, and they don't realize that doing that decreases their ability to monetize. Well, what do they do?
sentences.zh: 但他们还是不知道怎么变现，而且他们没意识到，这样做反而会降低自己的变现能力。那他们到底在干什么？

sentences.en: It just a game.
sentences.zh: 就只是一场游戏。

sentences.en: The platform monetization system.
sentences.zh: 平台的变现系统。

sentences.en: Like I have a few million followers and subscribers.
sentences.zh: 比如我有几百万粉丝和订阅者。

sentences.en: And on Instagram, if I were to just go with the reels bonus that you get, I'd get like 300 to $500 a month on Twitter.
sentences.zh: 在 Instagram 上，如果我光靠那个 Reels 奖金，一个月大概能拿 300 到 500 美元。

sentences.en: I think I get maybe like 2000 now, which isn't bad.
sentences.zh: 在 Twitter 上，我现在大概能拿 2000 左右，这倒不算差。

sentences.en: On YouTube.
sentences.zh: 在 YouTube 上，

sentences.en: I get around 10,000 a month and that's for someone with millions of followers.
sentences.zh: 我一个月大概能拿 10000 美元，而这还是一个有几百万粉丝的人的收入。

sentences.en: Sure, I could like live off of that if I really wanted to, but I businesses to run.
sentences.zh: 当然，如果我真想的话，靠这个也能活，但我有生意要经营。

sentences.en: I need to make a lot more money in order to build something valuable.
sentences.zh: 我需要赚多得多的钱，才能打造出有价值的东西。

sentences.en: So that means that I have to sell my own product or service, and then I can make 10 to 20 x that amount.
sentences.zh: 所以这意味着我必须卖自己的产品或服务，然后我就能赚到那个金额的 10 到 20 倍。

sentences.en: And if you're thinking of accepting sponsors or brand deals from someone, why wouldn't you just create your own version of it and then take all of the profits?
sentences.zh: 如果你在考虑接别人的赞助或品牌合作，那你为什么不干脆自己做一个自己的版本，然后把所有利润都拿走？

sentences.en: And you'd probably create it better in a way that better suited you?
sentences.zh: 而且你很可能做得更好，用一种更适合你自己的方式？

sentences.en: That's like how you start a good business nowadays, especially with a personal brand, is you take something that you use and you love and you make it better and tailor it to yourself.
sentences.zh: 这就是现在开启一门好生意的方式，尤其是有了个人品牌之后：你拿一个你自己在用、而且很喜欢的东西，把它做得更好，按你自己的需求去定制。

sentences.en: And since you are the niche, then you sell it to other people like you and you can find that tribe.
sentences.zh: 既然你自己就是那个细分市场，那你就把它卖给像你一样的人，你就能找到那个部落。

sentences.en: Now, since this isn't an entire course on content, even though I'll probably run a workshop at some point live on my Substack.
sentences.zh: 好，虽然这不是一门完整的内容课程——不过我之后可能会在 Substack 上开一次直播工作坊——

sentences.en: So again, subscribe to Substack.
sentences.zh: 所以再说一遍，去订阅 Substack。

sentences.en: But for now, I'll just give you the 80 over 20 of what to do.
sentences.zh: 但现在，我先给你一个二八法则的精华版。

sentences.en: First is just write down ideas like crazy, read more books, listen to podcasts, reflect on your life, and try to catch ideas that are unique and beneficial to is to immediately think of a pain point or benefit.
sentences.zh: 第一，疯狂写下各种想法，多读书、多听播客、反思你的人生，试着捕捉那些独特且对别人有用的想法，立刻去想一个痛点或好处。

sentences.en: Train your mind to think of why this idea is important to more than just yourself.
sentences.zh: 训练你的大脑去思考：为什么这个想法对别人也很重要，而不只是对你自己。

sentences.en: And then three save ideas that you like the structure of.
sentences.zh: 第三，收藏那些你喜欢的结构。

sentences.en: Have a folder in Eden where your ideas live and as a beginner, imitate the structure or framework of these with your own ideas as the topic.
sentences.zh: 在 Eden 里建一个文件夹存放你的想法，作为初学者，用你自己的话题去模仿这些内容的结构或框架。

sentences.en: Then you simply practice writing until it becomes second nature.
sentences.zh: 然后你就不断练习写作，直到它变成你的第二天性。

sentences.en: Now, when it comes to where you should post, you could just start with like a newsletter and a short form platform, or only start on Substack, or only start on Twitter and post all tweets and articles.
sentences.zh: 至于该发在哪里，你可以先从一份 newsletter 加一个短内容平台开始，或者只在 Substack 上起步，或者只在 Twitter 上发推文和文章。

sentences.en: But this is kind of my entire content ecosystem in a nutshell.
sentences.zh: 但我的整个内容生态，概括起来大概是这样。

sentences.en: I write the newsletter every week that can splinter into posts, and then the best posts can be used as like a carousel or the script for a short or real.
sentences.zh: 我每周写一篇 newsletter，它可以拆分成多条帖子，然后最好的帖子可以做成轮播图，或者短视频的脚本。

sentences.en: The newsletter turns into a YouTube video, and then all of that just feeds back into each other.
sentences.zh: 那篇 newsletter 会变成一期 YouTube 视频，然后所有这些内容又会互相反哺。

sentences.en: If you want to understand that as a whole, I'll leave another link in the description about the content ecosystem that you can look at.
sentences.zh: 如果你想整体理解这套逻辑，我会在简介里再放一个关于内容生态的链接，你可以去看。

sentences.en: Okay, so how do you actually use AI to make this process easier?
sentences.zh: 好，那到底怎么用 AI 让这个过程更轻松？

sentences.en: So if we look inside of the content section here you can see two prompts for tweets.
sentences.zh: 我们来看内容板块里面，这里有两个写推文的提示词。

sentences.en: Or these can just be considered posts because tweets are like the lowest common denominator where if you have a 280 character tweet that can really go to any platform or be used as the hook for real or whatever it is, I recommend getting really good at crafting tweet style posts first, because that will impact all of your other short form content.
sentences.zh: 或者你也可以把它们当成通用的帖子，因为推文是最小公分母，一条 280 字的推文可以发到任何平台，或者用来做短视频的开头钩子，我强烈建议你先练好写推文式的帖子，因为这会影响你所有其他短内容的质量。

sentences.en: And then for a newsletter.
sentences.zh: 然后是 newsletter。

sentences.en: This can also double as a podcast script or a YouTube script or whatever you'd like.
sentences.zh: 这个也可以同时当作播客脚本或 YouTube 脚本，随你怎么用。

sentences.en: Now, the way that you use AI well here, and the way that I created these prompts for you is I first took tweets or posts that I really liked, and then I plug them into AI and they said, hey, the breakdown.
sentences.zh: 这里用好 AI 的方式，以及我为你创建这些提示词的方式是：我先挑出我特别喜欢的推文或帖子，把它们扔给 AI，然后说，来分析一下。

sentences.en: Exactly why these work? What are the principles here?
sentences.zh: 它们为什么有效？背后的原则是什么？

sentences.en: What are the psychological tactics?
sentences.zh: 用了哪些心理学技巧？

sentences.en: Just teach me how to write these style of tweets.
sentences.zh: 直接教我写这种风格的推文。

sentences.en: And then I took that and I turned it into a prompt, and I refined it a bit so that the output was decent.
sentences.zh: 然后我把分析结果变成一个提示词，再稍微打磨了一下，让输出效果不错。

sentences.en: So here, in order for this prompt to work, you can just type a topic into this AI chat, or you can paste reference content here. So, newsletters that you've written or newsletters that you've liked or YouTube videos, you can paste it outside of this actual document and connect it to this chat.
sentences.zh: 所以在这里，为了让这个提示词生效，你可以直接在 AI 对话里输入一个话题，或者把参考内容粘贴进来。比如你写过的 newsletter、你喜欢的 newsletter，或者 YouTube 视频，你可以把它粘贴到这个文档外面，然后连接到这个对话里。

sentences.en: And it will generate potential tweet drafts that you can refined and make it sound like you.
sentences.zh: 它会生成一些推文草稿，你可以再打磨，让它听起来像你自己的声音。

sentences.en: Or you can start with the newsletter that you would post once a week on something like Substack.
sentences.zh: 或者你也可以从 newsletter 开始，每周在 Substack 这样的地方发一篇。

sentences.en: And you run through this.
sentences.zh: 然后跑一遍这个流程。

sentences.en: This is based off of my own structure and how I write, so there's a lot of knowledge.
sentences.zh: 这是基于我自己的结构和写作方式设计的，所以里面有很多干货。

sentences.en: I would recommend just reading this prompt, and you'll probably get an entire course worth of information.
sentences.zh: 我建议你直接读一遍这个提示词，你可能会获得相当于一整门课程的信息量。

sentences.en: But here, if you want it to sound a bit more like you, you can paste previous reference writing that you've had or if you wanted to emulate someone else's voice so you can start refining your own.
sentences.zh: 但在这里，如果你想让输出更像你的风格，你可以粘贴你以前写过的内容作为参考，或者如果你想模仿别人的声音来慢慢打磨自己的风格，也可以。

sentences.en: Because this provides just a starting point, a prototype that you can work from.
sentences.zh: 因为这只是一个起点，一个你可以继续加工的原型。

sentences.en: Then consider doing that.
sentences.zh: 那就考虑这样做。

sentences.en: And if you need help or just have questions, you can plug any of the outputs into this chat or any other chat and you can branch things off like this.
sentences.zh: 如果你需要帮助或者有问题，你可以把任何输出结果扔进这个对话或者其他对话里，然后像这样分支出新的方向。

sentences.en: But in this section right here, you can ask like, okay, how do I make this tweet better?
sentences.zh: 但就在这个板块里，你可以问：好，怎么让这条推文更好？

sentences.en: How do I actually write?
sentences.zh: 我到底该怎么写？

sentences.en: You can just ask questions to these videos or paste other videos in here if you'd like.
sentences.zh: 你可以直接对这些视频提问，或者把其他视频链接贴进来，随你。

sentences.en: So how you use AI with content isn't to just like write it and post it for you.
sentences.zh: 所以，用 AI 做内容，不是让它替你写完然后直接发。

sentences.en: It's to learn and understand faster.
sentences.zh: 而是用它来更快地学习和理解。

sentences.en: It's to see a post on social media, take that post, plug it into AI and say, hey, why does this work?
sentences.zh: 是让你在社交媒体上看到一个帖子，把它扔给 AI，问：嘿，为什么这个帖子有效？

sentences.en: And if I have this related idea, how can I take the principles from this social post that did extremely well and apply it to my own?
sentences.zh: 如果我有一个相关的想法，我该怎么把这个爆款帖子的底层逻辑提取出来，用到我自己的内容上？

sentences.en: And then after doing that, over time, it's like you're not taking a course to learn the principles, you're just learning them by doing.
sentences.zh: 这样做久了，你根本不用专门报课去学那些原理，你是在做的过程中直接学会的。

sentences.en: Because AI is so integrated with our workflows nowadays that that's just how you do things now.
sentences.zh: 因为 AI 现在已经深度融入我们的工作流了，这就是现在做事的常态。

sentences.en: And the same can be applied to something like a landing page.
sentences.zh: 同样的方法也可以用在落地页上。

sentences.en: If you're going to create a product or service, then why would you just try to write the landing page yourself without learning anything first?
sentences.zh: 如果你要做一个产品或服务，凭什么在不做任何学习的情况下，就直接自己硬写落地页呢？

sentences.en: Like normally you could take a course, but most people aren't going to do that either.
sentences.zh: 通常你可以去报个课，但大多数人也不会去报。

sentences.en: But now you can find a landing page from someone that you like that you know their stuff is working well, and you can just tell the AI to teach you how it works and then help you write your own landing page like that.
sentences.zh: 但现在，你可以找一个你喜欢的、你知道他东西卖得不错的人的落地页，直接让 AI 教你它是怎么起作用的，然后帮你写出一个类似的落地页。

sentences.en: So that leads into section three of this video.
sentences.zh: 这就引出了本视频的第三部分。

sentences.en: We had brand content and now we need product offer service or just what you sell in general.
sentences.zh: 我们讲了品牌、内容，现在需要讲产品、服务，或者笼统地说，你卖的东西。

sentences.en: So to reiterate that so far you have a few pieces of the one person business equation.
sentences.zh: 重申一下，到目前为止，你已经掌握了一人企业公式的几个要素。

sentences.en: First, you have a brand that illustrates your values and attracts the right kind of people.
sentences.zh: 第一，你有一个能展示你价值观、吸引对的人的品牌。

sentences.en: And number two, you have content that slowly builds trust over time and allows you to reach more people.
sentences.zh: 第二，你有能随着时间慢慢建立信任、并让你触达更多人的内容。

sentences.en: Simply put, you have people whose trust grows in you over time, and most businesses could only wish for that.
sentences.zh: 简单说，你拥有了一群对你信任度不断增长的人，这是大多数企业求之不得的。

sentences.en: Too many people try to build businesses nowadays and they don't actually try to get customers.
sentences.zh: 现在太多人想创业，但他们根本没真正去尝试获取客户。

sentences.en: They're like, I'm going to build this software, I'm going to build this thing.
sentences.zh: 他们会说，我要做这个软件，我要做那个东西。

sentences.en: They're really motivated.
sentences.zh: 他们动力十足。

sentences.en: But then when it comes time to actually do the business stuff, they're gone.
sentences.zh: 但一到真正要做商业落地的时候，人就消失了。

sentences.en: Now, this section of the video actually makes me kind of mad because I spent like five years learning this stuff, doing it all manually, and now the AI is a thing or it's so much easier.
sentences.zh: 说实话，讲到这部分我有点不爽，因为我花了大概五年时间学这些东西，全靠手动摸索，而现在 AI 出现了，一切都变得简单太多了。

sentences.en: It's so much like you get to shortcut all of the process.
sentences.zh: 你几乎可以跳过所有繁琐的过程。

sentences.en: But I don't take that for granted because I still have all of the knowledge and pattern recognition that would allow me to do it better than another person.
sentences.zh: 但我不会觉得理所当然，因为我仍然拥有所有的知识和模式识别能力，这能让我比别人做得更好。

sentences.en: So you're still building that along the way, and it's going to take you 2 to 5 years to actually reach the point of being able to, like, masterfully do all of this stuff.
sentences.zh: 所以你在这个过程中仍然在积累这些能力，而要真正达到能熟练驾驭这一切的程度，还是需要两到五年。

sentences.en: But you can start off on a great page by doing what we're going to talk about, because in today's world, you can have I do most of this for you.
sentences.zh: 但你可以通过我们接下来要讲的方法，从一个很高的起点开始，因为在今天，你可以让 AI 帮你搞定大部分事情。

sentences.en: If you know how to train the AI to use frameworks and knowledge from great marketers, salesmen and copywriters.
sentences.zh: 前提是，你知道怎么训练 AI 去运用那些顶尖营销人、销售和文案写手的方法论和知识。

sentences.en: So like I said before, right?
sentences.zh: 就像我之前说的，对吧？

sentences.en: You can take knowledge from an expert person, or you can take what they've done, like a social post that did really well.
sentences.zh: 你可以从专家那里获取知识，或者拿他们已经做出来的东西，比如一个爆款帖子。

sentences.en: You can pop that into I ask you to break down why this works, or teach me how to do it, or turn it into a guide, and then you can turn that thing into a prompt, which is what I did for you.
sentences.zh: 你可以把它扔给 AI，让它拆解为什么有效，或者教你怎么做，或者把它变成一个指南，然后你再把这个东西变成一个提示词，我就是这么为你做的。

sentences.en: But since I understand all the moving pieces, these prompts are very comprehensive.
sentences.zh: 但因为我自己理解所有环节，所以这些提示词非常全面。

sentences.en: So we have prompts for three things, but it helps to just know what we're doing here.
sentences.zh: 我们为三件事准备了提示词，但先搞清楚我们在做什么会更有帮助。

sentences.en: First, we need to create a detailed customer avatar.
sentences.zh: 首先，我们需要创建一个详细的客户画像。

sentences.en: This is something you'll keep safe and reference often whenever you're creating marketing materials.
sentences.zh: 这个东西你要好好保存，以后做任何营销素材时都要经常拿出来参考。

sentences.en: You need to save this somewhere, like in your workspace too is you create your first offer.
sentences.zh: 你需要把这个保存到某个地方，比如你的工作区，在你创建第一个产品的时候也要用到。

sentences.en: So using your customer avatar and offer creation principles, you create a product or service that they can't resist.
sentences.zh: 用你的客户画像和产品创建原则，打造一个他们无法抗拒的产品或服务。

sentences.en: And then three you turn both into compelling landing page draft because most people create a boring product and then just illustrate what the product does on their landing page and wonder why nobody wants it.
sentences.zh: 然后第三步，把两者转化成一个有说服力的落地页草稿，因为大多数人只是做了一个无聊的产品，然后在落地页上干巴巴地描述产品功能，还纳闷为什么没人想要。

sentences.en: So when you go through these three prompts, they're going to interview you extensively, and then they're going to spit out a customer avatar, an irresistible offer blueprint, and then landing page copy the act as first drafts that you can iterate on and ask questions to here by popping them into this chat, or just creating a new chat and chatting with them.
sentences.zh: 当你跑完这三个提示词，它们会对你进行深度访谈，然后输出一个客户画像、一个无法抗拒的产品蓝图，以及落地页文案，这些都可以作为初稿，你可以在此基础上迭代、提问，把它们扔进这个对话里，或者新建一个对话跟它们聊。

sentences.en: Now, the way this is structured is as so is when you run through the customer avatar generator.
sentences.zh: 这个流程的结构是这样的：你先跑客户画像生成器。

sentences.en: This the context of this chat plugs into this chat because you need your customer avatar information when you're creating an irresistible offer, and then your irresistible offer and customer avatar plug into this the landing page generation prompt.
sentences.zh: 这个对话的上下文会接入下一个对话，因为你在创建无法抗拒的产品时需要客户画像的信息，然后你的产品蓝图和客户画像又会一起接入落地页生成提示词。

sentences.en: Because how else are you going to write copy to a specific customer avatar about your offer right now?
sentences.zh: 不然你怎么可能针对一个具体的客户画像来写关于你产品的文案呢？

sentences.en: One thing I would recommend during this section is just make sure you actually open the outputs of these.
sentences.zh: 在这个环节我建议你做一件事：确保你真的打开这些输出内容看一看。

sentences.en: You can open things in a pain in Eden.
sentences.zh: 你可以在 Eden 里用分屏打开。

sentences.en: So I can open this up here, and I can edit it and look through it just to make sure everything is good.
sentences.zh: 我可以在这里打开它，然后编辑、浏览一遍，确保一切都没问题。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对吧。

sentences.en: This is also like where I do my writing and all of that stuff, but make sure it's good.
sentences.zh: 这也是我写作和做其他事情的地方，但一定要确保内容没问题。

sentences.en: Make sure it didn't hallucinate because you're still having to baby the AI here.
sentences.zh: 确保它没有产生幻觉，因为在这个阶段你还是得手把手盯着 AI。

sentences.en: But a final note here is that I can't guarantee that this is going to 100% work.
sentences.zh: 但最后要说的一点是，我没法保证这能 100% 奏效。

sentences.en: It's same thing with courses, the same thing with anything like knowledge, products or knowledge.
sentences.zh: 课程也是一样，任何知识类产品或者知识本身都是这样。

sentences.en: Giving out knowledge doesn't guarantee or result like a product or service does, and even products or services like physical products or services don't even guarantee results.
sentences.zh: 给出知识并不能保证结果，不像一个产品或服务那样，而且即便是实体产品或服务也不一定能保证结果。

sentences.en: You get a skin care product and it may work for you.
sentences.zh: 你买了一个护肤品，它可能对你有效。

sentences.en: It may help your skin, but if you don't address the underlying root cause of what's causing you not to get results regardless of the skin care product or the knowledge that you have, then you're probably not going to succeed.
sentences.zh: 它可能对你的皮肤有帮助，但如果你不去解决那个导致你无论用什么护肤品、掌握什么知识都无法获得结果的底层根本原因，那你大概率还是不会成功。

sentences.en: Some people just don't have the identity they had.
sentences.zh: 有些人就是没有那个身份认同。

sentences.en: They haven't done the inner work to overcome their fear of uncertainty or failure.
sentences.zh: 他们没有做过内在功课去克服对不确定性或失败的恐惧。

sentences.en: They haven't done all these things.
sentences.zh: 这些事情他们都没有做。

sentences.en: There's so many different moving variables in one little piece of knowledge isn't going to save you.
sentences.zh: 有太多不同的变量在变化，一小块知识救不了你。

sentences.en: This has to be a lifelong journey of wanting it.
sentences.zh: 这必须是一段你真心想要的终身旅程。

sentences.en: And another thing is that I frankly still, and probably for the foreseeable future, isn't that good yet.
sentences.zh: 另外一点是，坦白说，AI 现在还不够好，而且在可预见的未来可能还是不够好。

sentences.en: It just can't do these things for you.
sentences.zh: 它就是没法替你完成这些事情。

sentences.en: It's missing something, and we don't know what that something is.
sentences.zh: 它缺少了某种东西，而我们不知道那是什么。

sentences.en: It's definitely not more intelligence.
sentences.zh: 那肯定不是更多的智能。

sentences.en: Once people can open, open claw or another agent thing and make hundreds of thousands of dollars, the next day, which is probably going to be impossible at any given moment, because that's not how the market works.
sentences.zh: 一旦人们能打开 Claude 或者其他什么智能体，第二天就赚几十万美元——这在任何时候大概都是不可能的，因为市场不是这么运作的。

sentences.en: That's how that's just like a commodity.
sentences.zh: 那样的话就成了一种大宗商品。

sentences.en: If anyone can do it immediately, then it's not going to work.
sentences.zh: 如果任何人都能立刻做到，那它就不会奏效。

sentences.en: If it works for a small period of time, then that's called an exploit and it's going to be squashed really fast.
sentences.zh: 如果它在短期内奏效了，那叫漏洞利用，而且会很快被封堵掉。

sentences.en: You will still have to learn, you will still have to practice, and most importantly, you will still have to iterate when something doesn't work until it does work.
sentences.zh: 你仍然需要学习，仍然需要练习，最重要的是，当某件事不奏效时，你仍然需要不断迭代，直到它奏效为止。

sentences.en: So I hope that was helpful for you.
sentences.zh: 希望这些内容对你有帮助。

sentences.en: I hope those prompts help you a lot.
sentences.zh: 希望这些提示词能帮到你很多。

sentences.en: I hope you learned something and I hope you continue to learn something, because the learning in this video actually happens by doing the prompts and implementing them.
sentences.zh: 希望你学到了东西，也希望你继续学下去，因为这期视频真正的学习，是在你实际去用那些提示词、去执行的时候发生的。

sentences.en: So that's the video.
sentences.zh: 这期视频就到这里。

sentences.en: Let me know what you want to see next in the comments.
sentences.zh: 下期想看什么，评论区告诉我。

sentences.en: Devin checks the comments, so say hi to Devin while you're down there and he'll hit you with a little heart or a like.
sentences.zh: Devin 会看评论，留言的时候顺便跟他打个招呼，他会给你点个赞或者一颗心。

sentences.en: And with that, I'll see you in the next video. Bye.
sentences.zh: 就这样，下期视频见。拜。
